homer/app/infra/RedosPatternDetector.kt#: `end` is indexOf(close, open + 3) with open >= 0, so it is -1 or at least 3: `end < 0` and `end <= 0` agree on every value it can take.

With `close - open - 1` the scan resumes two characters early, inside the interval: only its last digit or comma and the closing '}' are re-read, plain characters the scanner's default branch skips, so the verdict is the same.
`close` is indexOf('}', open) where pattern[open] is '{', so it is -1 or greater than open >= 0, never 0: `close < 0` and `close <= 0` agree.
The extra outer iteration (a == branches.size) runs an empty inner loop (`a + 1 until size`) and reads no branch, so the result is the same.

homer/app/runners/external/ExternalShell: Both `capError(sink, kill)` calls of `doneResult` carry this key; the first is killed by ExternalRunnerSessionTest's cap trip landing before a timed-out result, so only the re-check after `requireCompleteOutput` is left. That re-check is defence in depth, not a branch a test can drive: it closes the window in which a chunk append trips the cap after the previous check has read it, and appends arrive on the output route's own `Dispatchers.IO` thread rather than this coroutine's, so no test can schedule one into a window that suspends nowhere — the race is real, it is just unschedulable. The check stays a documented tripwire; the verdict a test can pin — a cap trip reported as `OutputCapExceededException` with `kill.byCap` and the `[HOMER] Output cap exceeded` stderr marker, never a clean result — is pinned by ExternalRunnerSessionTest's cap tests.
homer/app/runners/queue/RunnerClaimQueue: `dropSettled()` is a race guard, not a step of the scan: every settle path takes its own request out of the deque — `remove` on the expiry and cancellation CASes, and the `pending.remove` right after the claim CAS — so the call only reclaims a request another thread settled between that CAS and its removal, a window no test can schedule. Without it the scan still sees no settled request, so the claims it serves, the deque's bound and the reservations it frees are unchanged, all pinned by RunnerClaimQueueTest.

The mutated return is the early `return emptyList()` for a consumer whose instance has no affinity identity: Collections.emptyList() is an equal empty list, and no caller reads the returned list's identity, so only the lift's effect — the waiters it wakes — is observable, and that is pinned by RunnerClaimQueueTest.

The same race guard as in `claimMatch`, seen from the bound: `dropSettled()` here only reclaims a request another thread settled between its CAS and its own removal, and without it `pending` holds no settled request in any interleaving a test can schedule, so the `maxPending` refusal it precedes is unchanged. The bound itself — a settled request freeing its slot for the next run — is pinned by RunnerClaimQueueTest.
homer/app/runners/ssh/WorkspaceSync.kt#c: The containment throw cannot fire while `isPlainFileName` passes: a name with no separator, no NUL and neither `.` nor `..` always resolves to a direct child of `base`, so removing the check changes no observable behaviour and no test can kill it. The alternative, a production seam letting a test reach the containment check with the name guard bypassed, was tried and reverted: testability does not justify new surface in a security guard, so the check stays a documented tripwire whose composite the property test pins.
